title: How a project hands itself to you today

body.html:
1. Context pass. Before each phase, the agent reads the project's prior art on that topic and writes down what it found. On prod-app: the build plan, SetHero V2, studio and byod-reference.
  2. The plan. One plan file plus one file per phase: what's committed, how it's checked, and its gate.
  3. The wishlist. Everything not yet committed (ideas, call notes, paper cuts, design suggestions) in one untidy file, read at each phase's start and gate.
  4. The board. Each decision is a card with the agent's recommendation and why. Where it's unsure, a look-closer card says where to look. Obvious calls skip the card and go on a list you can object to.
  5. You answer, and the answers go back to the agent. Today that's copy and paste.
  6. The agent builds, writes the outcome into the phase's "As built", and takes the card off.
  7. The story is told in a sprint review every two weeks, and design handoffs go to Claude Design at phase starts and gates.

checks.text: What follows is prod-app's experience, roughly two weeks and about 60 decisions. A second project would test which parts are general and which are Horizon's.
Recommendations with a reason let you decide in seconds: almost every answer you sent was my recommendation, and the ones that weren't came with a reason.
"Look closer" and the settled list kept no-brainers off your plate.
On prod-app, the context pass caught three would-be mistakes: the storage design was already documented, V2 had the empty-table problem, and studio (not byod) was where the AI work lived.
Copy-paste both ways, and old notes came back. "How do V2, studio and the docs handle this?" arrived three times: your notes outlived the cards they were written on.
Your notes were often questions. The answer came back as a rewritten card, with no thread linking question and answer.
I edit the board's HTML by hand, and broke it twice: once losing a card, once leaving a shape the next edit didn't expect.
The high-level view is scattered. You asked "sprint review updated?", "anything not committed?", "memory updated?", "did we film all of it?": status the board couldn't answer.
Nothing tracked what I'd committed to. An approved settled item (the "Stopped" toast) went unbuilt for a day until I noticed.
Questions for other people had no home: the one for Luke lived in the sprint review.

notePrompt: Anything I've got wrong about how it works for you? (optional)
summary: The loop is general; every example and every lesson below comes from prod-app (SetHero Horizon), the one project that has run it so far. Review is meant to carry the same loop to every project in Switchboard.
